notes: gqlstatus is the pinned root-cause GQLSTATUS from ROOT_CAUSE_CODES in scripts/ce_error_fixtures.py (maintained from neo4j/neo4j 2026.09 CE acceptance-test/GQLSTATUS sources; per-case source_url). gqlstatus_wire is the top-level GQLSTATUS the live driver sees.
message is the live CE text with the position decoration stripped; CE canonicalizes string literals to double quotes in the attempted-graph echo.
Where the live text differs from the wording quoted in ADR-0116/ADR-0117 the case is listed in the script's DIVERGENCES; CE text is authoritative.

cases.message: No database is corresponding to `graph.byElementId(4:00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000:n1)`. Verify that the elementId is correct.
cases.status_description: error: syntax error or access rule violation - referenced database not found. No database is corresponding to `graph.byElementId(4:00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000:n1)`. Verify that the elementId is correct.
cases.note: The middle segment must be a well-formed UUID; a non-UUID segment such as 'doesnotexist' fails earlier in ElementIdDecoder with an IllegalArgumentException before reaching this error.

cases.message: The following clauses are not allowed on a system database: WITH.
cases.status_description: error: syntax error or access rule violation - unsupported request. 'WITH' is not allowed on the system database.
cases.note: Live CE 2026.09 chains 42001 -> 42N17 -> 42NA9; the wire message is 'The following clauses are not allowed on a system database: WITH.' — the §4 whitelist's composability completion (ADR-0116 §4, 2026-11-04).

cases.message: The `USE` clause is not required for administration commands. Retry your query without the `USE` clause, and it will be routed automatically.
cases.status_description: error: syntax error or access rule violation - invalid USE clause. The USE clause is not required for administration commands. Retry your query without the USE clause, and it will be routed automatically.
cases.note: CE's auto-routing rejection for any USE clause on a database-administration command (bare or composed, UNION arm included); CypherLite keeps `USE system` + administration command accepted as a recorded divergence.

cases.message: No write operations are allowed on this database. The database is in read-only mode on this Neo4j instance.
cases.status_description: error: syntax error or access rule violation - read-only database. The database is in read-only mode.
cases.note: Requires the server to be started with server.databases.read_only=neo4j (Docker: -e NEO4J_server_databases_read__only=neo4j) on a pre-initialized store; see the module docstring for the two-pass setup.

cases.message: Query cannot conclude with CALL (must be a RETURN clause, a FINISH clause, an update clause, a unit subquery call, or a procedure call with no YIELD).
cases.note: Captured 2026-09-30 on the read-only server (server.databases.read_only=neo4j): CE rejects a read-only top-level CALL { } at semantic-check time with 42N71 (a query may not conclude with CALL), before read-only enforcement runs. CypherLite classifies a top-level CALL { } as a write outright and fails 42N18 instead — the outcome matches (CE does not allow read-only top-level CALL { } on a read-only database either), only the code and layer differ. CypherLite's behavior is pinned by system_ontologies_rejects_top_level_call_subqueries_with_42n18 in cypherlite/cypherlite/tests/namespace.rs.
